unit.name: Language model pretraining and supervised fine-tuning
unit.description: Connects reinforcement learning to LLM alignment by explaining next-token pretraining, the helpfulness gap, and supervised fine-tuning.
unit.summary: The RLHF section begins by recapping that language models are pretrained with next-token prediction over text, producing a model that can continue prompts but is not necessarily helpful [ts=5433s] [ts=5451s]. The lecture identifies two alignment problems: online pretraining data does not reflect users asking for help, and the pretrained model has no direct concept of good, polite, or helpful behavior [ts=5537s] [ts=5573s]. Supervised fine-tuning addresses this by collecting human prompt-response pairs and continuing supervised training on demonstrations of helpful behavior [ts=5628s] [ts=5662s]. SFT is still limited because human-written responses are expensive, the initial InstructGPT-style dataset was small, and imitation of examples is not the same as preference optimization [ts=5753s] [ts=5801s].

key_points.text: Language-model pretraining uses next-token prediction: given preceding text, the model predicts the next token and is updated by gradient descent.
A pretrained language model is trained to continue text, not necessarily to answer user questions helpfully.
Another alignment gap is that a pretrained model has no direct concept of being good, polite, or helpful.
Supervised fine-tuning builds a dataset of human prompt-response pairs and fine-tunes the pretrained model on those pairs.
SFT teaches imitation of human-written helpful behavior, but not direct optimization of human preferences.

kp_catalog.name: Language-model pretraining alignment gap
kp_catalog.description: Next-token prediction creates capable text continuation models but not necessarily models that answer helpfully, politely, or safely.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The LM helpfulness gap motivates RLHF, but it is not itself an RL prerequisite.

kp_catalog.name: Supervised fine-tuning for LLM helpfulness
kp_catalog.description: Fine-tuning a pretrained LM on human prompt-response demonstrations to imitate helpful responses.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: SFT is described as learning from human-written demonstrations but only imitation, not preference optimization [ts=5628s] [ts=5801s].
